title: introduce-residency-assertion-broker-and-rbac-assertion-cache
author: Diego Morales
release_notes: Add residency assertion broker (X-Redwood-Residency-Ticket) and an RBACv2 assertion cache with configurable TTL. Feature gated behind security.enableResidencyBroker. Audit emits compact cache-hit events.
description:
Motivation: For customers subject to data residency rules, KMS selection and RBAC decisions must be deterministic and fast. Prior deployments evaluated residency late and repeated full RBACv2 policy evaluations for high-frequency operator flows, adding latency and verbose audit noise. This PR implements a residency assertion broker that canonicalizes region claims into a signed residency ticket early in the request path, and a small RBACv2 assertion cache to de-duplicate policy evaluations for repeated operator actions while preserving auditability.

Summary of changes: 1) pkg/residency/broker: new broker that ingests tenant claims, runs residency rules, and issues a signed header X-Redwood-Residency-Ticket containing region, issued_at, ttl_ms, and a provenance signature. 2) pkg/auth/assertioncache: LRU-backed assertion cache for RBACv2 decisions with configurable ttl_ms, max_entries, and an eviction_reason metric. 3) internal/router: routing layer consumes X-Redwood-Residency-Ticket to choose KMS proxy endpoints and short-circuits provider discovery when a valid ticket is present. 4) internal/kms: KMS client validates ticket provenance and enforces region pinning when the ticket is trusted. 5) docs/security/residency-broker.md and docs/ops/runbooks/residency-ticket-failures.md added. 6) test/integration/residency_ticket_flow_test.go: end-to-end scenario that simulates cross-region operator sessions and audit sinks. Feature is off by default and gated by security.enableResidencyBroker.

Commit highlights (top-level): - b5d8a1c: initial broker scaffolding, ticket encoder/decoder - c3f4b27: assertion cache implementation + eviction metrics - 9f7d21e: router and kms client wiring + helm toggle - a2b44f0: integration test and test fixtures - e8c0f9b: docs, migration note, runbook

Changed files (high level): pkg/residency/broker/broker.go (new), pkg/auth/assertioncache/cache.go (new), internal/router/router.go (modified), internal/kms/client.go (modified), docs/security/residency-broker.md (new), test/integration/residency_ticket_flow_test.go (new)

Review notes and thread: - Nina Zhao: "Good to emit a minimal ticket; avoid embedding full policy. Please ensure ticket signature key material rotation is covered." Response: "Ticket payload reduced to {region, issued_at, ttl_ms, nonce, issuer}. Added key rotation section to docs and linked KMS rotation playbook." - Evan Kim: "Cache looks sound; add singleflight to avoid duplicate backend policy evaluations under high concurrency." Response: "Added singleflight locking per cache key to prevent stampedes; added metrics.assertion_cache.concurrent_blocked." - Priya Patel (security): "Audit sinks may receive the ticket; we need guidance for redaction for external sinks." Response: "Added audit-sink config to strip ticket.proof fields and documented recommended retention windows. Cache-hit audit events emit only a fingerprint and not the full decision payload (audit.kind=assertion_cache_hit)."

CI timeline: initial pipeline ran 2026-01-29. Lint and unit tests passed except a flake in integration. Integration test initially failed due to non-deterministic clock skew handling; fixed by adding verifier timestamp slack and test harness clock control. Final pipeline: all checks green. Security scanning noted a hardening suggestion to limit default TTL to 120000 ms; default TTL updated to 2 minutes in config and documented.

Operational considerations: - Config: security.enableResidencyBroker=false by default; security.residencyBroker.default_ttl_ms=120000; security.assertionCache.max_entries=5000 - Metrics: metrics.residency.tickets_issued, metrics.residency.tickets_rejected, metrics.assertion_cache.hits, metrics.assertion_cache.misses, metrics.assertion_cache.evictions_reason - Logs: broker emits structured logs when tickets issued and when verifications fail (level=warn). - Runbook: added steps to diagnose ticket verification failures (check signer key, verify clock skew, fallback to provider discovery). - Rollout guidance: enable in staging for a small tenant cohort, monitor tickets_rejected and cache evictions, then expand. Operators with custom KMS proxies should update routing to accept X-Redwood-Residency-Ticket or rely on fallback behavior.

Backward compatibility: Default behavior unchanged when feature disabled. When enabled, routing favors ticket-driven KMS selection; this can be rolled back by toggling the feature flag. No public API schema changes beyond an optional header.

Related work: ENG-2744 (router simplification) and SEC-510 (audit consolidation). This PR focuses on an early assertion pattern and a small cache to reduce repeated expensive evaluations while preserving verifiability for audits.

Merge outcome: Merged via squash on 2026-02-04 after approvals from Nina Zhao and Priya Patel. Post-merge: 72-hour staging soak showed no regressions; a minor follow-up was created to add a helper library for verifying tickets in third-party sinks (ENG-2761).
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative in scope; all risky changes are feature-gated and documented.
